children: CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV, Financials), the AI cloud infrastructure company based around high-performance computing, climbed around 2.5% in premarket trade Friday as investors reacted to another strong signal for AI demand.

Nebius Group and IREN also advanced, gaining approximately 2.4% and 1.4%, respectively. This was the catalyst from Oracle. Cloud infrastructure sales increased 121% year-over-year to $7.4 billion and the business inked more than $30 billion in new cloud contracts connected to AI.

That's important beyond Oracle. CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all investing extensively in Nvidia GPUs, electricity and data centers. The whole investing thesis rests on the idea that clients require additional computer capability.

Recent company updates have added some momentum. CoreWeave announced a field engineering solution to help companies deploy AI models. Nebius partnered with Palantir, and IREN moved on with its planned 2-gigawatt Texas data-center project.
Wall Street still sees a lot more upside. Average analyst estimates from TipRanks suggest roughly 73% upside for IREN, 56% for CoreWeave and 26% for Nebius.

Oracle's results are good news for investors, but the real test is returns on capital. The companies now need to prove that the high demand for standard artificial intelligence can outpace the huge cost of creating the infrastructure needed to support it.

title: Oracle's AI Cloud Growth Lifts CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN
